questions.prompt: Why does the graph of y = x³ - 4x have a turning point between x = 0 and x = 2?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does the graph of y = x³ - 4x have a turning point between x = 0 and x = 2?

choices.text: Because y is positive between 0 and 2 (for example y(1) = 3), so the graph must come back down to 0 at x = 2.
Because the graph crosses the x-axis at x = 1, halfway between 0 and 2, and a graph turns at every crossing.
y is 0 at x = 0 and at x = 2 and negative between them (for example y(1) = -3), so the graph must turn back up somewhere between them.
Because every cubic with a positive leading coefficient turns at x = 1, which lies between 0 and 2.

questions.correct_answer: y is 0 at x = 0 and at x = 2 and negative between them (for example y(1) = -3), so the graph must turn back up somewhere between them.
questions.grading_note: A continuous graph that leaves 0, goes negative, and returns to 0 has a lowest point in between. The others state false facts.

questions.prompt: Why does the end behavior of V(x) = x(12 - 2x)² not matter for the box made from a 12-in sheet?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does the end behavior of V(x) = x(12 - 2x)² not matter for the box made from a 12-in sheet?

choices.text: The context uses only 0 < x < 6, so the behavior for large |x| is never used.
Because V(x) = x(12 - 2x)² has no end behavior at all.
Because the volume of the box is always 128 cubic inches.
Because x must be negative for the box, so large positive x is never used.

questions.correct_answer: The context uses only 0 < x < 6, so the behavior for large |x| is never used.
questions.grading_note: End behavior describes inputs outside the meaningful interval. The others are false: V does have end behavior, the volume is not constant, and x cannot be negative for a box.
